task_instance: Acting as the claude-permissions skill: for a sample project, permit the write command 'terraform apply' and the read-only command 'flux get' in the project's Dippy config, and permit the xlsx Skill in the project's .claude/settings.local.json, following the skill's duplicate-check, read-only-defaults, and auto-mode [ASK] conventions.
evidence: The skill's core deliverable is managing Claude Code permissions by editing plain-text config files (Dippy config/.dippy and settings.json) -- no code execution is needed to produce it. Built a realistic sample: a global Dippy config stand-in (home_dippy/config) with set-default-ask plus read-only allows and no terraform-apply/flux rule; a project sample_project/.dippy with two prior allows; and sample_project/.claude/settings.local.json with Read and WebFetch. Performed the request: (1) duplicate-checked 'terraform apply' and 'flux get' against both configs -- neither was covered by an existing rule; (2) added 'allow flux get' (read-only, per the skill's Flux auto-permit list) and 'ask terraform apply "[ASK] ..."' (write/destructive -> ask, tagged [ASK] so it reaches a human in auto mode), placed after the allows so last-match-wins ordering applies; (3) added 'Skill(xlsx)' to the settings.local.json permissions.allow array (Skill is a settings.json permission, not a Bash/MCP one, so it correctly does not go in Dippy). Verified by re-reading both files: the .dippy rules are syntactically correct and correctly ordered, and settings.local.json is valid JSON (braces/brackets balanced, array elements quoted and comma-separated) -- confirmed by inspection in lieu of the skill's optional 'jq .' step. Files produced: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/b273891e-4b73-5af7-9840-fc512af93809/scratchpad/real2_work/r246/home_dippy/config, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/b273891e-4b73-5af7-9840-fc512af93809/scratchpad/real2_work/r246/sample_project/.dippy, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/b273891e-4b73-5af7-9840-fc512af93809/scratchpad/real2_work/r246/sample_project/.claude/settings.local.json. The skill's bundled config.example and dippy-with-auto-fallback.sh were present next to SKILL.md and used as format reference only. The skill's optional verification extras (running dippy to test a command, jq JSON validation) require code execution and were not available, but they are not the core deliverable.
